subject: Clarify mid-cycle GPU-hour allocation during migration surge
messages:
From: Alex Ramos <aramos@brightcart.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: BrightCart Finance <finance@brightcart.com>
Date: Sun, 01 Aug 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Unexpected GPU-hour spike mid-cycle — please advise

Hi Marissa,

We just received the July invoice and are seeing a ~38% increase in GPU-hour charges compared to our historical weekly average. This jump appears to align with the migration window we ran on Jul 29–30, but the magnitude seems larger than the additional jobs we triggered.

Can you share a per-instance / per-pool breakdown for the 07/25–08/01 window (timestamps in UTC preferred), plus any autoscaling events or burst policy triggers? We need line-item detail to reconcile with our bookkeeping before we can approve payment.

I've attached the usage export we pulled from our side for reference. Happy to hop on a quick call if that helps.

Thanks,
Alex Ramos
Head of Ops, BrightCart
aramos@brightcart.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

Attachment: brightcart_usage_export_20270725-20270801.csv (CSV, 78KB)

From: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Ramos <aramos@brightcart.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, grace_oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 02 Aug 2027 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected GPU-hour spike mid-cycle — please advise

Hi Alex — thanks for the heads up and for sending the export. I'm sorry for the hassle; we'll get you a clear breakdown ASAP.

Quick context so we're aligned: BrightCart is on a Dedicated pool (dc-us-west2-gp-large) with a burst policy that allows up to 30% additional capacity for short spikes. Around 2027-07-29T22:00Z we recorded several short-lived autoscale events; my initial read is that a combination of ephemeral cluster spin-ups and a couple long-running batch jobs during your migration caused the greater-than-expected hours.

Action plan:
- Ben (billing infra) will pull a per-instance hour report, with tags (tenant_id, cluster, instance_type) and show autoscale triggers and burst utilization.
- Grace (CS) will correlate that to your onboarding/migration ticket to map which job groups belong to the migration vs normal traffic.
- I'll package the CSVs and a short reconciliation memo you can attach to your invoice approval workflow.

Ben / Grace — can you pull the instance-level export (UTC) and a run manifest (container start/stop events) for 2027-07-25 through 2027-08-01 by EOD tomorrow? Alex, we'll include timestamps and request ids so you can match rows to your logs.

If it's easier, I can schedule a 30-min sync with your finance team tomorrow morning PST — let me know what works.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

From: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Alex Ramos <aramos@brightcart.com>
Cc: grace_oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 03 Aug 2027 11:43:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected GPU-hour spike mid-cycle — instance-level export attached

Hi all — digging in and attaching the raw exports. Summary first:

Summary (short):
- Total billed GPU hours 07/25–08/01 (UTC): 12,384.5 hours
- Baseline (previous 7-day avg): 8,962.1 hours
- Delta: +3,422.4 hours (38.2%)
- Root cause: 2 factors — (A) migration batch job group ID bc-mig-20270729 spawned 42 long-lived nodes (avg runtime 6.2 hrs) that were tagged incorrectly, so they were not covered by your scheduled "maintenance" tag; (B) autoscale burst triggered on two occasions due to a short-lived synthetic load from the migration traffic (07/29T21:55Z and 07/30T02:10Z), each ~18 minutes, which inflated continuous-hour accounting because instances were billed at the hourly granularity when they overlapped hour boundaries.

What I'm attaching:
- brightcart_instance_hourly_20270725-20270801.csv (columns: timestamp_utc, instance_id, pool, instance_type, tag, tenant_id, hours_billed, trigger_reason)
- redwood_run_manifest_20270730.txt (simple run log: instance_id -> container start/stop, job_group_id)

A few notes on billing mechanics so it's clear how we got to the delta:
1) Hourly rounding: if an instance runs across an hourly boundary we round up to the next 15-minute bucket, which can create small per-instance deltas that add up across hundreds of nodes.
2) Tagging mismatch: bc-mig-20270729 nodes were created with tag "temp" instead of your usual "maintenance" tag; maintenance-tagged nodes can be excluded from billable compute under your contract during approved migration windows — the mis-tagging is the primary lever here.
3) Burst policy: bursts are allowed but are billed separately under rule 2.2 of your SOW; the two short bursts amounted to ~210 billed hours in total due to rounding and overlap.

Proposed remediation:
- We can credit the hours for any instance matching job_group_id bc-mig-20270729 and with tag "temp" if BrightCart confirms these were internal migration runs and wants them excluded. That's ~2,940 billed hours.
- For the remaining ~482 hours attributed to burst rounding, we propose a one-time goodwill credit of 240 hours to split the delta.

Next steps for you (Alex):
- If you confirm bc-mig-20270729 should be excluded, reply here and we'll prepare a credit memo for the invoice.
- If you want us to pursue an additional operational change (preventing tag drift + auto-exclude for maintenance windows), we can open an engineering change request and propose a short-runbook.

Attachments: brightcart_instance_hourly_20270725-20270801.csv, redwood_run_manifest_20270730.txt

- Ben Carter
Billing Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

Attachment stubs: brightcart_instance_hourly_20270725-20270801.csv (CSV, 210KB); redwood_run_manifest_20270730.txt (TXT, 45KB)

From: Alex Ramos <aramos@brightcart.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: BrightCart Finance <finance@brightcart.com>
Date: Wed, 04 Aug 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected GPU-hour spike mid-cycle — instance-level export attached

Thanks Ben — this is helpful and much more granular than we had. Two quick clarifications before we proceed to credits:  

1) For the bc-mig-20270729 job_group_id nodes, can you include the container request_ids (or the top-level request_id) in the export so we can cross-reference with our orchestration logs? We want to be 100% sure these are migration-only workloads.

2) On the proposed goodwill split: BrightCart will accept the credit for the mis-tagged migration nodes (we'll provide written confirmation once our infra cross-checks). For the burst rounding, we'd like Redwood to provide the hour-by-hour overlap table (UTC) for the two burst periods so we can audit the rounding math — if it looks like the rounding rules created more than 50% of the billed delta for those intervals, we'll accept a 50% split as you suggested; otherwise we'll ask for full reversal of the rounding-related hours.

If you can add the request_ids and the hour-overlap table to the package, we can sign off and get the invoice processed this week. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

—Alex
